declared_deviations.what: no separate terminal Adj event is emitted
declared_deviations.why: spec §3 recomputes after every registration and the vendored P0 Harness does exactly that inside each registration event, but it exposes no public Adj emitter; the import writes through the registration API only and never forges a log line, so the terminal adjudication is the state after the last event

declared_deviations.what: imported FCL problem records use SpawnTrigger.SEED
declared_deviations.why: the vendored enum has no 'import' member; 'seed' is the only trigger that does not assert an in-graph derivation. The clean fix is an enum addition, requested rather than papered over

declared_deviations.what: research problems use SpawnTrigger.RESEARCH with empty criteria
declared_deviations.why: the vendored enum has the member and §12 is exactly this path, but the trigger is not part of the v1.3 enum text; criteria stay empty because no instantiated commitment id is a criterion

declared_deviations.what: document-local depends refs are dropped, not turned into dep edges
declared_deviations.why: at node granularity they would be dep self-loops, i.e. cycles; toposort rejects them and a self-loop asserts nothing the author declared

declared_deviations.what: a self-targeting objection mints no warrant
declared_deviations.why: a Dung self-attack means 'this argument is self-defeating', which is not what an intra-document caveat asserts; minting it would flip two labels for reasons that have nothing to do with the evidence

declared_deviations.what: an objection against a record this import reified as a warrant attacks that warrant's validity node, not the node artifact
declared_deviations.why: spec §1 closure: attackers of a validity node attack the warrant and every carrier of it, so criticism of a criticism keeps its force instead of collapsing into a plain edge onto the carrier

declared_deviations.what: the retargeting rule above has ONE exception: an objection against a criticism carried by the SAME artifact is not retargeted
declared_deviations.why: the §1 closure lifts an attack on a validity node onto every carrier of the warrant, and for an intra-document criticism of a criticism that carrier is the objector itself, so retargeting would mint a self-attack through the closure and make the artifact self-defeating - which is not what an author asserts by qualifying their own earlier objection. `objection.o4` against `o1`/`o2` is exactly this case; it is dropped, not retargeted, and counted under its own code so the loss is visible rather than silent

declared_deviations.what: an FCL `claim` record maps to no spec construct
declared_deviations.why: a claim asserts content without proposing a test, so it is neither an observation-valued commitment nor a criticism nor a problem; it survives in the artifact body and in the FCL-1 document artifact, and is reported here because `uptake_refs_unmapped` covers only the claims the author put in `uptake`

multi_arm_framing: This scope contains 2 arms (bare, mini_prose) whose declared commitment surface is prose and 1 arm (mini_fcl) whose surface is FCL-1. A prose commitment surface is never parsed, so no warrant, no attack edge and no refuted label can arise from a prose arm under this import. The distribution of statuses across arms is therefore a property of the carrier this importer reads, not a comparison between the arms. Any cross-arm reading is root's, not this instrument's.

problems.description: I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

The material does not say why the third flatmate has started avoiding the chore conversations; feeling criticized or ganged up on, being outvoted two-to-one, disengagement from the flat, and causes unrelated to chores are all open, and they call for different responses.

This design trades flexibility for clarity: whole-domain ownership is more brittle under shifting schedules than the input account's weekly swap planning. Deputy defaults (a named fallback per area when the owner is away) and monthly rather than weekly adjustment are partial answers, not a resolution.

Private preference rankings can be gamed: someone may overstate how much they mind an area to capture an easy domain. Periodic rotation of the least-preferred domain, or allowing paid substitution, are candidate mitigations; neither is tested here.
The input account's commitment surface is not supplied in this exchange, so uptake can address only its exposed body (ad92700706f3372d); its records, if any, cannot be used or objected to from here.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#r11): Hold structural exits open as legitimate endpoints rather than as failures — splitting a cleaner three ways, shrinking the shared surface, or renegotiating the living arrangement — to be weighed only after a fair, minimal, jointly adopted system has been tried in good faith and the friction persists.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#r2): Confirm every new chore agreement in writing at the moment it is made — task, concrete standard, deadline — in a place all three can see.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#r4): Ask the avoidant friend one-on-one, without accusation, what makes the chore conversations hard, before designing or proposing any system on their behalf.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#r6): Adopt an explicit swap rule: a schedule change triggers a proposed swap in the shared note, never a silent lapse.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#r8): Replace ad-hoc chore talks with a short, scheduled weekly check-in covering assignments against actual schedules, swaps, and schedule changes — mostly forward-looking rather than retrospective.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/rival#r3): Allocate each common area as an owned domain: one owner, responsible end to end, answerable to a written floor and free to exceed it as they please.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/rival#r4): Put the specification where the work happens rather than where the talk happens: a checklist inside the cupboard door, taped to the bin lid, on the bathroom mirror, plus one gap-filler rule agreed once — where nothing is written at the spot, the default standard is X.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/rival#r6): Rotate the chair: the member who convenes, records and adjusts the arrangements serves a week or a month at a time, so each of the three is sometime designer and sometime subject.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/rival#r8): Where tolerances genuinely differ, trade across domains rather than enforce uniform standards: a lower common floor; or cleaning load swapped against the admin nobody wants (bills, shopping, landlord calls); or a small rent adjustment.
